mentl/ebcba74:
No .mn changed — tree green at census 0. This banks a measurement that
changes rung 3's acceptance criterion.

The movers line counts "schemes the final judges differently than the trial
published", and rung 3's acceptance has been stated as movers -> 0. Measured
with the decl's cell published instead of a Frozen snapshot, it does not
fall: 474 -> 1594 (branch band raised to 4096 so the run reached far enough
to report).

That is not a regression, it is the metric losing meaning. With a snapshot,
divergence between the passes is hidden INSIDE the snapshot — the trial's
frozen view stops tracking and the count sees only what the comparison
happens to catch. With a live cell there is nothing to hide it: the cell IS
current truth, so every decl the final touches reads as a mover.

So the stage contract's sequencing is right and its ratchet is not. movers ->
0 arrives from DELETING the second pass (step 4, "the trial/final collapse
FOLLOWS, not precedes"), never from making two passes agree — and reading the
ratchet as a gate ON the live-cell step inverts the order, refusing the
landing that makes it reachable. The honest gate for that step is the fixpoint
plus the census, with movers re-derived after the trial pass is gone.

mentl/ebf8c52:
The bank Ruling 3. A MultiShot perform of ANY arity now rides the k1
spine: its args evaluate at the yield site in the enclosing frame (the
already-computed prefix — the k's hole swallows the whole perform, so
the remainder never re-evaluates them) and ship as a transient
word-slot record in $yield_args, the strictly-additive 4th global. The
lifetimes decide the design: k is durable (immutable, called N times,
composed onto — the persist=memcpy object); args are transient
(consumed once by the matching driver dispatch inside the same unwind).
Argless yields emit byte-identical.

The driver reads each op's arity LIVE off multishot_ops_of — now
(name, arity) pairs through the typed handler_arm_arity projection
beside its sibling accessor; one decider, three readers — and pushes
(record, k, arg0..argN-1) from fixed word offsets. The arm's signature
has carried (__k, args...) since k1; nothing changes at the arm. The
yield-site mint uses the clobber-safe parking discipline: the record
ptr lives in the per-site $yargs_<h> local (the only slot inner arg
emissions cannot touch) and each arg value parks in $state_tmp only
after its own emission completes. A non-word op arg meets the arm's
loud call mismatch (the callsite-result-width family), never a silent
truncation.

mentl/ebcae2c:
$list_extend_to extended with the canonical bump-allocator in-place
realloc trick: when the list is at the heap-top (no allocations
since this list was made), grow it in-place via $perm_alloc instead
of allocating a fresh list and copying.

Pre-substrate, every buffer-counter caller (cfn_walk in emit,
ec6_emit_args, etc.) hit O(N²) reallocations: they wrote count
back to offset 0 after list_extend_to, overwriting the doubled
capacity that list_extend_to set via $make_list. Each subsequent
list_extend_to read the now-small count from offset 0 and
reallocated again. For wheel-scale N≈20K closures this exhausted
the 1.5 GiB perm cap and trapped at perm_alloc.

Empirical: bisecting wheel termination at + lower:
  Pre-substrate:  exit=134 (TRAP), 87,285 stderr lines, 0 WAT
  Post-substrate: exit=124 (timeout), 4,524 stderr lines, 0 WAT

Trap → graceful timeout. Stderr drops 19× because the seed gets
much further before the timeout fires. The structural O(N²) leak
is closed; remaining timeout is just runtime cost.

The in-place trick: when list_end (logical end of list data) aligns
to heap_ptr, route through $perm_alloc(extra*4) — respects perm
cap, advances heap_ptr, returns padding/new-slot region. Logical
list addressing keeps coming from the original pointer; the new
slots come pre-zeroed (WASM linear memory untouched-bytes = 0).

Symmetric to GMP / glibc / V8 zone allocators' realloc-from-heap-
top pattern.

Companion: $cfn_walk_list (emit/main.wat) gets a HEAP_BASE guard
mirroring $cfn_walk's existing one — productive-under-error when
upstream lower passes a sub-HEAP_BASE pointer.

two-top/eb0ebea:
Adds an `AppScreen { Title, InMatch }` state machine so "back to lobby" has
somewhere to go, and models the match lifecycle explicitly.

- Title = no ggrs `Session` → bevy_ggrs idles the sim at frame 0 (its
  schedule_systems resets RollbackFrameCount/snapshots every frame while
  session-less — the same state online sits in before a peer connects). The
  title overlay shows the arena + a start prompt.
- InMatch = match entities exist and a fresh `Session` drives the rollback
  sim. On entry, `spawn_match` spawns the two duelists + walls + the selected
  arena's props (fixed order → bit-identical entity ids) and, couch-only,
  installs a fresh SyncTest session (so the frame count restarts at 0). On
  exit, `despawn_match` tears the whole match down and drops the session,
  returning to the clean idle.
- MatchOver summary overlay: winner banner + final score + "throw to play
  again" (the in-sim rematch from 5.5a) and, couch-only, "Esc for lobby".
- Start (Space/Enter/tap) Title→InMatch; Esc (couch, MatchOver) InMatch→Title.

Couch boots into Title; online is untouched — it boots straight into InMatch
and its existing perform_swap path inserts the P2P session on connect (the
lobby FSM owns online teardown, so back-to-lobby is couch-only).

Refactors: `setup` now spawns only the persistent scene (camera, floor,
control legend); match-entity spawning moved to `screen::spawn_match`. Render
gains an `ArenaProp` marker on every prop so a whole arena tears down in one
query (also sets up arena-switching in 5.5b-ii). `bevy_state` feature added.

The session insert/remove/re-insert lifecycle is grounded in the bevy_ggrs
0.21 source (clean reset when no session present); runtime GUI flow is
operator-batched like the visual/audio gates. Gate: 363 tests, clippy
--all-targets clean, app binary links. No sim change → determinism intact.

tokensafe/eb09d66:
5 independent optimizations to reduce degraded results and extend
effective daily capacity from ~6,600 to ~11,000 checks at zero cost:

1. Adaptive token age: 2-phase getSignaturesForAddress (limit:2 probe
   → limit:100 if needed). Saves ~900 RPC credits/check.
2. Degraded result caching: 30s TTL instead of skip. Prevents RPC
   hammering on transient failures.
3. withRetry helper: single retry with 500ms delay for transient errors
   (timeout/429/503/ECONNRESET). Applied to token-age, top-holders,
   metadata.
4. CLMM LP lock skip: Raydium CLMM pools skip LP lock detection
   (positions, not fungible LP tokens). Saves 1-2 RPC calls.
5. Conditional PDA Phase 2: program resolution only when concentration
   high enough to affect scoring (top10>30% or top1>10%).
